footer.tokensSaved: The tokens and keys you enter there are saved, so you do not have to create them again the next time you build an app. They live in one document in your own App Builder database, encrypted so that only you can read them — not even someone you share that database with.

list.heading: Your apps
list.intro: Describe what you need, and it gets built, published, and added to Haven.
list.readOnly: This App Builder database is read-only for you, so finished apps are not kept in this list. Everything still works — copy the app’s address before you leave the page.

empty.title: Build your first app
empty.body: Tell us what your team is missing. An AI developer writes it, it gets published to the web, and Haven installs it — you can keep changing it afterwards.

confirm.title: Remove “{label}” from this list?
confirm.hint: This deletes only what the App Builder saved about the app, here in its own database. Nothing else is touched: the project stays on GitHub, the published app keeps running on Cloudflare, any Cursor agent stays where it is, and Haven keeps it installed. Building a new app with the same name will not bring this row back — the builder stops when it sees that GitHub project already exists. The published app stays reachable at its address. To get the row back, restore the deleted document in Haven’s App Builder database.

address.hint: Anyone you send this address to can add the app to their own Haven. “Save as file” keeps a copy of the app definition, for a Haven that cannot reach the address.

labels.iterate: Hand it to the AI again

hints.create: Nothing has been created yet — this runs the whole thing.
hints.commit: The GitHub project exists but the starter code was not named for your app yet. This carries on from there.
hints.publish: The code is on GitHub. This puts it on the web and adds it to Haven.
hints.build: The web address is reserved but the app never went live. This builds it.
hints.install: The app is live. This asks Haven to install it.
hints.iterate: Starts a Cursor agent on the app again.

links.heading: Maintain it
links.repoHint: Everything the AI writes lands here.
links.agentHint: Ask for changes and watch it work.

builds.heading: Publishing
builds.none: Cloudflare has not built this app yet.
builds.hint: Every change pushed to GitHub publishes itself.

agent.needsKey: Needs a Cursor key — add one under “Connections and setup”. Or clone the repository and change it yourself, with whatever tool you like.

intro.withAi: This takes a couple of minutes. We create the project, publish it to the web, and add it to Haven, then set the AI developer to work on it. You can watch each step.
intro.withoutAi: This takes a couple of minutes. We create the project, publish it to the web, and add it to Haven. You can watch each step.
intro.starterOnly: What you get is the starter app, live and installed — the code is then yours to change, by hand or with any AI tool.

newApp.narrowAccess: You chose to pick repositories yourself, so after the project is created you will need to allow Cloudflare (and Cursor) to see it on GitHub. We will stop and tell you when.

finished.hint: Everything about this app — its address, the code, publishing, the AI developer — is on its own page from now on.

newAppForm.title: What do you want to build?
newAppForm.purpose: Describe your app the way you would explain it to a colleague. The AI turns this into working software — no technical wording needed.

name.label: Name your app
name.hint: This is the name you will see in Haven.

description.label: In one sentence, what is it for?

task.label: Describe what it should do
task.placeholder: Let people write notes, tag them, and search across them. One screen with the list of notes, one for writing. Everyone on the team can see and edit them.
task.hint: This is the brief the AI works from — the more concrete, the better. Think about who uses it, what they see on screen, and what they can do. You can always ask for changes afterwards.

slug.label: Short name for the web address
slug.hintAfter: — this is the link you email to colleagues so they can add it to their Haven.

privateCode.label: Keep the code private
privateCode.hint: Recommended. The app itself is still reachable by anyone with the link; this only hides the source code from strangers.

id.label: Database id
id.hint: The store this app writes to. Each app gets its own, so two apps never share documents by accident.

label.label: Name shown in Haven
label.hint: A readable name for the database. This can be the app name, with spaces and capitals.

permissions.label: What the app may do
permissions.hint: Read access is always included. You can turn any of these off before you build.

header.title: Set up once, then build apps
header.purpose: Your apps need somewhere to live. Connect the three services below and approve a couple of installs — after that, creating an app is a name and a button.

setup.intro: GitHub keeps the code and Cloudflare hosts it; both are free. Cursor is the AI developer that writes the app, and its cloud agents need a paid plan. You can leave Cursor out: the app is still created and published, and what you get is an ordinary Git repository — edit it yourself, or point Claude Code, Codex or any other tool at it.

access.title: How much access to give
access.purpose: Every app you build gets its own new GitHub project, and Cloudflare and Cursor have to be allowed to see it.

all.label: All repositories — recommended
all.hint: Approve once, and every future app is covered. Building an app becomes a single button. If that feels broad, use a GitHub account you keep for this.

selected.label: Pick the repositories myself
selected.hint: Narrower, but every new app needs two extra approvals on GitHub before it can be published — the builder will tell you when.

installs.title: Approve the installs

intro.lead: Each link opens GitHub in a new tab.
intro.selected: Choose the repositories you want each one to see.

builder.hint: Lets this builder create the new project and make its first commit. Only needed if you connected GitHub with the button above — a token you pasted yourself already carries its own permissions.

cloudflare.hint: Lets Cloudflare read the project so it can publish it, and re-publish on every change.

cursor.hint: Lets the AI developer read and write the project. Skip it if you would rather change the code yourself, or with a different tool.

installs.note: We cannot see these installs from here, so nothing on this page will tick itself off. If a build later fails because something was not approved, we will say so and bring you back.

finish.blocked: Connect GitHub and Cloudflare above first. Those two are what create and publish your app.

connect.title: Accounts
connect.storageHint: Stored in one document in your App Builder database, encrypted for you personally. Nobody else can read it, not even someone you share that database with.
connect.ephemeralWarning: These connections will only last until you close this page. To have them remembered, install the App Builder from Haven's App Store — or add it by URL — instead of opening it directly.

github.scopeHint: Grants permission to create a new project and make the first commit — not to read the repositories you already have. Revoke it any time in GitHub's application settings.
github.tokenHintBeforeScope: — the link opens GitHub's form with the one permission we need,
github.tokenHintAfterScope: , already ticked. Check that it is, choose how long the token should last, press
github.tokenHintAfterGenerate: , then copy the value into the field above. GitHub shows it only once.
github.orgSummary: Create apps under an organization instead
github.ownerHint: Leave this alone and your apps are created under your own account. An organization works too, but the installs you approved for yourself do not cover it — you have to approve them there as well.

cloudflare.consentHint: Opens Cloudflare's own consent screen. It asks for the Workers permissions the builder needs and nothing else, and the access token is exchanged in this page wherever Cloudflare allows it.
cloudflare.waitingHint: Finish signing in in the Cloudflare tab. If that tab says to return here, copy its address and paste it below.
cloudflare.tokenHintPermissions: , and add these two permissions: Workers Scripts → Edit and Workers Builds Configuration → Edit. Then copy the token into the field above.
cloudflare.profileHintIntro: Create it on the page that link opens —
cloudflare.profileHintTail: too, but those cannot switch on automatic publishing, so the next page would stop with an error.
cloudflare.accountSelectHint: Your token can act on several — this is the one your apps go in.
cloudflare.accountIdFallbackIntro: You can enter it below instead: open
cloudflare.accountIdFallbackTail: and copy the long code out of the address bar — the part right after
cloudflare.accountIdHint: Normally there is nothing to fill in here — pasting the token above reads the account from it.
cloudflare.accountIdManualHint: Pasting a token again reads this from the token. Change it by hand only if you know which account you want.

cursor.keyHintTail: . Used to start a cloud agent on the new repository. Cursor's API cannot be called from a browser and has no consent flow, so this one key is sent to the builder host for that single call. It is never given to the agent itself.
cursor.optionalHint: Leave it empty if you would rather write the code yourself, or use another tool on the repository — Claude Code, Codex, your editor. Nothing else here depends on it.
